THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 13.08.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO. 1051/2020 ON THE FILE OF THE VIII ADDITIONAL SCJ AND ACMM, MEMBER, MACT, BENGALURU SCCH-5,
AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.26,43,400/- WITH INTEREST AT 9 PERCENT P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THIS DAY, DR. CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Heard Sri.B.S.Karthikeyan, learned counsel who represents Smt.Ramya H.N. learned counsel on record for appellant and Sri.Syed Zaheeruddin Bareed, learned counsel who is representing respondents No.1 and 2.
2.

Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru, in MVC No.1051/2020 dated 13.08.2021.
3.

The respondents herein (hereinafter referred to as 'the claimants' for brevity) moved an application claiming compensation in the light of the death of their son Shashikanth in a motor vehicle accident.
The claimants projected themselves to be the parents of the deceased.

The Tribunal subjecting the evidence of PWs.1 to 5, Exs.P8 to P30, RW1 NC: 2024:KHC:20346-DB Exs.R1 to R9 to scrutiny, came to a conclusion that the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.26,43,400/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
A direction was issued to the respondent to deposit the entire amount within two months from the date of the order.
Aggrieved by the liability fixed, the respondent therein has preferred the present appeal.

4. On this day, making his submission with regard to merits of the matter, learned counsel Sri.Karthikeyan submits that the deceased Shashikanth was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet and also by keeping a big cotton box on the petrol tank i.e. between him and the handle and thereby he could not control the handle and he himself went and hit the bus and thus the accident occurred.

Learned counsel states that as the driver of the bus was not at fault, the Tribunal ought not to have fastened liability upon the respondent, but it indeed ordered the respondent to pay the The Managing Director vs Sri Jagadeesh Singh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103811411/
2 compensation and therefore, aggrieved by the said order the present appeal is preferred.
5.

sentences.text:
Per contra, the submission of the learned counsel for the claimants before this Court is that the accident occurred NC: 2024:KHC:20346-DB due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus only and therefore, the compensation that was ordered to be paid has to be paid by the appellant herein.
6.
Learned counsel for the appellant placed much reliance upon the evidence of RW1 who is none other than the driver of the bus who was driving the vehicle when the accident occurred.

The evidence of RW1 is that the motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA.41-EM-6928 driven by its driver without wearing helmet keeping one big cotton box on his bike rode the bike without following traffic rules and regulations that too at a high speed, came from opposite side and dashed against his bus and thus the accident occurred.
When examination made in chief in respect of RW1 is taken into consideration, the same would be in consonance with the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellant before this Court.

However, a perusal of the impugned order goes to show that the same person i.e. RW1 gave statement before the Depot Manager that the deceased Shashikanth was riding his motor cycle while using his mobile phone.
However, such a defence is not taken before the Tribunal.
What prompted RW1 to take different versions before different forums is not made clear.

If the evidence of NC: 2024:KHC:20346-DB RW1 has to be considered, it is incumbent on his part to make consistent statement before all the authorities and all the persons who recorded his statements/evidence.
That apart, it is not in dispute that police laid charge sheet against RW1 and that the contents of the charge sheet till now remains unchallenged.

Except the evidence of RW1,
there is no material on record to show that the deceased was riding the motor cycle either in a rash and negligent manner or without wearing helmet or by keeping the cotton box on his bike.
Without concrete evidence in respect of these facts, the appellant cannot succeed to establish his version that the deceased was at fault.

It is specifically mentioned in the impugned order that RW1 admitted in his cross examination that he gave statement before the depot Manager that the deceased Shashikanth was riding his motorcycle while using his mobile.
If that version was true, RW1 ought to have stated same fact before the Court, but he did not do so, and he projected a different version.
Having considered all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability against the appellant.
In the light of the foregoing discussion, we are of the view that there are no grounds to interfere with the findings given by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal by taking into consideration all the factual aspects which are brought before it by way of evidence, has come to a just conclusion.
Thus, the appeal stands dismissed without costs.

Sd/-
JUDGE Sd/-
